To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

dietary nitrate and its metabolite nitrite are essential components of the human diet, and their intake is associated with a reduction in the risk of cardiovascular disease, including myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke.
dietary NO3−/NO2− supplementation increases the bioavailability of NO and improves endothelial function in humans.

the nitrate and nitrate/nitrite levels in a large sample of commercial baby foods are higher than previously reported and that the levels are not consistent with the recommendations of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of dietary nitrate and its metabolite nitrite, on the cardiovascular and metabolic health of humans.
the role of dietary nitrate in the prevention of CVD.
the role of nitrate and its metabolite nitrite in the cardiovascular system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitrate, nitrite, and NO are all essential for life and health.
dietary nitrate and/or nitrite supplementation may have beneficial effects on vascular health, and that this may be mediated by a combination of mechanisms.
dietary nitrite and nitrate are safe for consumption at the levels present in the food chain and that they are unlikely to contribute to any significant health risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nitrate/nitrite content of foods is a major determinant of the nitrosation of secondary amines, and this nitrosation is a major source of the nitrosoamine content of foods.
the nitric oxide system is a very complex and multifaceted system, and that the nitric acid pathway is not only a pathway for the production of NO.
the nitrite and nitrate levels in our food supply are safe and not likely to be associated with any health risks.

nitrite and nitrate are not bad for you.
